topic_title: Indian Space Programme (ISRO), Launch Vehicles, Satellite Systems, Remote Sensing & DRDO Defense Technologies
syllabus_mapping: Indian Space Programme: Evolution from INCOSPAR to ISRO - Launch vehicles: SLV-3, ASLV, PSLV (Workhorse of ISRO), GSLV Mk-II, LVM3 (GSLV Mk-III), Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV), Reusable Launch Vehicle (RLV-TD) - Satellite Orbits: LEO, Polar Sun-synchronous, Geostationary (GEO), Geosynchronous (GSO) - Landmark space missions: Chandrayaan series (Chandrayaan-1, 2, 3 lunar south pole landing), Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan), Aditya-L1 (solar observatory), Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme, XPoSat, NISAR - Satellite Navigation: NavIC (IRNSS) and GAGAN - Remote Sensing and Earth Observation (IRS series) applications in agriculture, disaster monitoring, water resources, urban planning, and fisheries - Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO): Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP: Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul, Nag) - Advanced missile systems: Agni-V (MIRV capability - Mission Divyastra), BrahMos supersonic cruise missile, Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD) shield, Anti-Satellite (A-SAT) Mission Shakti, indigenous combat aircraft (LCA Tejas), and nuclear submarine INS Arihant.

content.text: The Indian Space Odyssey (ISRO), Planetary Exploration, Satellite Navigation, and DRDO Strategic Defense Architecture

India's space and strategic defense sectors epitomize technological leapfrogging—transforming from modest post-independence sounding rocket experiments at Thumba to achieving interplanetary exploration, human spaceflight capabilities, and a credible nuclear triad deterrence shield.

content.text: 1. ISRO Launch Vehicle Fleet & Orbital Capabilities

content.caption: Comparative Architecture of ISRO's Launch Vehicle Fleet
rows: PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle)
4 Stages: Alternate Solid (HTPB) and Liquid (UH25 + N2O4 Vikas engine) stages. Stages: S1 (Solid) -> L2 (Liquid) -> S3 (Solid) -> L4 (Liquid).
~1,750 kg into 600 km Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit (SSPO); ~1,400 kg into Sub-GTO.
'Workhorse of ISRO'; launched Chandrayaan-1 (2008), Mars Orbiter Mission (2013), and record 104 satellites on PSLV-C37 (2017).
GSLV Mk-II
3 Stages: S1 (Solid core + 4 liquid strap-ons) -> L2 (Liquid Vikas engine) -> CUS (Indigenous Cryogenic Upper Stage using LH2 + LOX).
~2,250 kg into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).
Mastered indigenous cryogenic technology; primarily deploys INSAT/GSAT communication and meteorological satellites.
LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3 / GSLV Mk-III)
3 Stages: 2 massive S200 solid strap-ons -> L110 core liquid stage (twin Vikas engines) -> C25 high-thrust cryogenic upper stage (CE-20 engine).
~4,000 kg into GTO; ~8,000 kg into Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
'Baahubali' rocket; launched Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3, OneWeb satellite constellations, and human-rated for Gaganyaan.
SSLV (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle)
3 Solid Stages + Velocity Trimming Module (VTM) liquid stage for precise orbital injection.
Up to 500 kg into 500 km planar/low Earth orbit.
Designed for rapid commercial turnaround (assembled in under 72 hours by a small team) for small satellite constellations.

items: Chandrayaan-3 (2023): Historic soft-landing of the Vikram Lander and Pragyan Rover on 23rd August 2023 near the lunar south pole (designated 'Shiv Shakti Point'); made India the 4th country to soft-land on the Moon and the 1st near the south pole; August 23 declared 'National Space Day'.

Aditya-L1 (2023-24): India's maiden solar observatory placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrangian Point 1 (L1, ~1.5 million km from Earth); continuously observes solar coronal mass ejections (CMEs), solar wind, and space weather without eclipse interruptions.

Gaganyaan Programme: India's indigenous human spaceflight mission aiming to send a 3-member crew into a 400 km LEO for a 3-day mission and safely return them to Indian waters; demonstrated Test Vehicle Abort Mission (TV-D1) and humanoid robot 'Vyommitra'.

NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation / IRNSS): Autonomous regional satellite navigation system comprising 7 operational satellites (3 geostationary and 4 geosynchronous); provides Standard Positioning Service (SPS) with <10m accuracy over India and 1,500 km beyond borders.
NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar): Dual-frequency L-band and S-band radar satellite to map global land surface deformations, glacier movements, and forest biomass with millimetric precision.

content.text: 3. DRDO Strategic Defense Missiles & The Nuclear Triad

content.caption: Key Missiles under IGMDP and Strategic Systems
rows: Agni-V (Mission Divyastra)
Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM); 3-stage solid propellant with composite rocket motor casing.
Canisterized road-mobile system; equipped with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicles (MIRV) warheads; completes India's land-based nuclear deterrence.
BrahMos
Supersonic Cruise Missile (Indo-Russian joint venture); 2-stage (solid booster + liquid ramjet); speeds up to Mach 2.8–3.0.
290 km (extended to 450–500+ km post-MTCR accession)
'Fire and Forget' precision strike; deployable from land, sea, submarine, and Su-30MKI fighter jets.
Akash & Akash-NG
Surface-to-Air Missile (SAM); ramjet rocket propulsion; multi-target interception capability.
25 km (Akash) / 70 km (Akash-NG)
Protects vulnerable military air bases and vital installations against maneuvering enemy jets and cruise missiles.
Mission Shakti (A-SAT)
Anti-Satellite kinetic kill weapon tested on 27th March 2019.
Low Earth Orbit (~300 km)
Demonstrated direct-ascent kinetic kill interception of an active LEO satellite; placed India alongside USA, Russia, and China in outer space defense.
INS Arihant (SSBN)
Indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine equipped with K-15 (Sagarika, 750 km) and K-4 (3,500 km) SLBMs.
Underwater endurance limited only by food/crew endurance
Completes India's survivable second-strike sea-based nuclear triad leg, fulfilling the 'No First Use' doctrine.

content.text: Part A: Mains Analytical & Descriptive Questions

items:
Explain the scientific objectives and technological significance of the Chandrayaan-3 mission. How does soft-landing near the lunar south pole enhance India's global space standing? (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Detail the payload configuration: Propulsion Module, Vikram Lander, and Pragyan Rover; explain key technological improvements over Chandrayaan-2 (expanded landing zone 4x2.4 km, hazard detection cameras, reinforced landing legs, increased fuel margins); detail on-site scientific discoveries: ChaSTE measuring subsurface thermal gradient, ILSA recording lunar seismic activity, and LIBS confirming elemental Sulphur (S) in lunar regolith; evaluate the geopolitical and commercial impact: establishing ISRO as a premier space agency, positioning India for the Artemis Accords, and boosting commercial launch contracts under NewSpace India Limited (NSIL).

Describe the architectural components of NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation). How does it ensure strategic autonomy compared to foreign GPS dependency? (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Explain the 7-satellite constellation architecture (3 in Geostationary Orbit at 32.5°E, 83°E, 129.5°E, and 4 in inclined Geosynchronous Orbit); describe dual service offerings: Standard Positioning Service (SPS) for civilians and encrypted Restricted Service (RS) for defense forces; contrast with dependence on US GPS which was denied to India during the 1999 Kargil Conflict; assess civilian and strategic integration: mandatory NavIC compliance in commercial 5G handsets, tracking of maritime fishing vessels (especially near Sri Lankan/international maritime boundaries in AP/TN), and precision guidance for missile systems.

Critically evaluate India's Nuclear Triad capability. How does the induction of nuclear-powered submarines like INS Arihant reinforce India's 'No First Use' nuclear doctrine? (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Define the nuclear triad as the capability to launch nuclear weapons from land (Agni ICBMs), air (Mirage 2000, Rafale, Su-30MKI), and sea (SSBNs); analyze the vulnerability of land and air legs to preemptive first strikes by an adversary; explain why SSBNs (INS Arihant, INS Arighaat) provide the most survivable, stealthy second-strike platform; connect this survivability directly to India's Nuclear Doctrine (1999/2003) which mandates 'No First Use' (NFU) and 'Massive Retaliation' causing unacceptable damage.

content.text: Part B: Screening / Prelims Objective Questions

items:
Q1. Which day has been designated as 'National Space Day' in India to commemorate the historic lunar south pole landing of Chandrayaan-3?
(a) July 14
(b) August 15
(c) August 23
(d) October 22
Correct Answer: (c) August 23 [Explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi declared August 23 as National Space Day to celebrate Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touchdown on the Moon in 2023.]

Q2. The successful test-firing of the Agni-V missile equipped with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicles (MIRV) technology in March 2024 was conducted under which mission code-name?
(a) Mission Shakti
(b) Mission Divyastra
(c) Mission Sudarshan
(d) Mission Trishul
Correct Answer: (b) Mission Divyastra [Explanation: Mission Divyastra was the first flight test of the indigenous Agni-V missile with MIRV technology capable of delivering multiple warheads to distinct targets.]

Q3. How many operational satellites constitute the core space segment constellation of India's regional navigation system NavIC (IRNSS)?
(a) 5 satellites
(b) 7 satellites
(c) 12 satellites
(d) 24 satellites
Correct Answer: (b) 7 satellites [Explanation: NavIC consists of a constellation of 7 satellites: 3 in Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) and 4 in Geosynchronous Orbit (GSO).]

Q4. Which cryogenic rocket engine developed indigenously by ISRO powers the C25 upper stage of the heavy-lift LVM3 (GSLV Mk-III) rocket?
(a) CE-7.5
(b) CE-20
(c) Vikas-2
(d) Semi-cryogenic SCE-200
Correct Answer: (b) CE-20 [Explanation: The CE-20 cryogenic engine powers the upper C25 stage of LVM3, while CE-7.5 powers the Cryogenic Upper Stage of GSLV Mk-II.]

Q5. BrahMos, the world's fastest supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India and Russia, is propelled in its cruise stage by which type of engine?
(a) Turbojet engine
(b) Liquid Ramjet engine
(c) Scramjet engine
(d) Solid Rocket Motor
Correct Answer: (b) Liquid Ramjet engine [Explanation: BrahMos uses a solid propellant booster motor in the first stage and a liquid ramjet engine in the second stage to sustain Mach 2.8+ supersonic flight.]
